video.title: Don't Swing AT the Ball on the Overhead

classification.reason: The coach provides actionable cues and drills to throw the hand toward a consistent spot while allowing natural internal shoulder rotation to slap the ball across the body.

problem.title_as_question: Why shouldn't you swing directly at the ball on an overhead?
problem.definition: Players often try to direct their hand path straight at their intended target on the overhead, which misaligns with natural shoulder rotation and degrades wrist stability.

symptoms.description: Mishitting or shanking the ball due to reduced fault tolerance at contact.
Wrist feels structurally weaker during contact when trying to hit straight toward the target.
Hand throwing path directly aligned with the ball's final flight line without an angular offset.

causes.statement: Internal shoulder rotation naturally propels the racket to slap across the body at an angle offset from the hand's throwing path.
Varying the hand throwing trajectory to direct different spins allows returners to read and anticipate shots early.
Delaying contact to hit straight in the direction of the hand throw places the wrist in a weaker structural position near the end of the swing range.

angles.summary: Shoulder internal rotation naturally slaps the racket across the body relative to where the hand throws.
Projecting the hand throw path onto the back fence shows a 10 to 30 degree offset from the ball's actual landing target.
Andy Roddick and Ben Shelton throw their hands toward the opposite service box while internal rotation sends the ball to their target.
Believing that optimal overhead power and accuracy come from throwing the hand directly at the ball target.

solutions.summary: Identify a comfortable target spot in the opposite service box where your hand naturally throws on serves and overheads.
solutions.external_goal: Locate the comfortable hand throwing spot in the opposite service box.

solutions.summary: Disguise shot directions by throwing the hand to the same spot while rotating the forearm slightly earlier, later, more, or less.
solutions.external_goal: Throw hand to the exact same spot while altering shot targets through forearm rotation.

solutions.summary: Throw your hand toward your chosen spot while feeling the racket naturally slap the ball 15 to 20 degrees to the left.
solutions.external_goal: Allow the racket to slap the ball 15 to 20 degrees to the left of the hand throw direction.
